title: Physics — Mission 1: The Catapult Rig
description: The engineering club's catapult keeps missing its target ahead of the fair. You have one afternoon to fix the launch angle and force calculations before judging starts.

hana.name: Coach Hana Osei
hana.description: Can eyeball a trajectory before the numbers even finish printing.

milo.name: Milo
milo.description: Thinks 'more force' is always the answer.

protractor.name: Protractor
protractor.description: Measures the catapult's launch angle precisely.

trial_log.name: Trial Log
trial_log.description: Recorded launch speeds and landing distances from earlier tests.

elements.text: The rig keeps overshooting. Before we touch the tension again, we need to understand the forces and the trajectory.
Let's just crank the tension down until it stops overshooting!

options.text: "Let's check the trial log first — the launch angle and initial velocity will tell us exactly what to change."
"Just crank the tension down and see what happens."

elements.text: Good, you pulled the trial log. Let's work through the trajectory properly.
Guessing at the tension wastes every remaining trial. We need the actual numbers.

config.question: Milo wants 'more force' to fix the overshoot. According to Newton's second law, F = ma, what actually happens if force increases but mass stays the same?
config.explanation: F = ma means acceleration is directly proportional to net force when mass is constant — more force means more acceleration, likely worse overshoot.

config.prompt: Order these steps for solving a projectile motion problem, first to last.

items.text: Break initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components
Solve for time of flight using vertical motion
Use time and horizontal velocity to find the range

config.prompt: Milo: "For maximum range on level ground with no air resistance, what launch angle in degrees is ideal?"

elements.text: Angle's corrected, trajectory checks out. The rig is ready for judging.
It'll fly, roughly. Next time, work the kinematics before touching the tension.

elements.prompt: The rig is set. What now?

options.text: Show Milo how launch angle and velocity components determine range.
Log off. The rig works, that's enough for today.

elements.text: So it was never about more force, it was about the angle and the components the whole time. Wild.

ending.title: Kinematics Hero
ending.description: Fixed the catapult's trajectory and taught the club the physics behind it.

ending.title: Rig Ready
ending.description: The catapult works. The deeper lesson can wait until tomorrow.
